questions.learningObjective: Select y to replace a place complement

stimulus.body: The architect states that the team will go to the site. The note must replace the place with the correct pronoun.

questions.stem: Which sentence in the architect's brief correctly uses y to replace a place complement?

options.text: L'equipe le va pour inspecter le chantier.
options.misconception: uses le instead of y for a place

options.text: L'equipe en va pour inspecter le chantier.
options.misconception: uses en instead of y for a place

options.text: L'equipe y va pour inspecter le chantier.
L'equipe la va pour inspecter le chantier.
options.misconception: uses la instead of y for a place

questions.explanation: Y replaces a place complement, while en replaces a quantity or de complement; the other pronouns do not mark place.

questions.stem: Which sentence in the architect's brief correctly uses faire meaning to have something done?

options.text: L'architecte fait l'equipe peindre la facade.
options.misconception: misplaces the agent in the causative construction

options.text: L'architecte fait la facade peindre par l'equipe.
options.misconception: misplaces the object in the causative construction

options.text: L'architecte fait peindre la facade par l'equipe.

questions.explanation: The causative construction is faire plus infinitive plus object plus agent; misplacing elements would break the standard pattern.

questions.topic: Causative faire and laisser
questions.learningObjective: Explain why faire differs from laisser in a causative sentence
questions.stem: Explain why faire differs from laisser in a causative sentence in the architect's brief.

answer.exemplar: Faire causes an action to happen, while laisser permits it; using one instead of the other would change whether the subject imposes or allows the action.

questions.explanation: Faire imposes an action, whereas laisser allows it; swapping them would alter the subject's control.

options.misconception: uses personne for a thing

L'architecte a rien signe.
options.misconception: omits ne before the verb

options.text: L'architecte n'a signe rien.

questions.explanation: Ne rien refers to things and follows the verb, while ne personne refers to people; reversing them would misstate what is negated.
